title: Backcasting from 'Org Pivots Are Legible': Mapping the AI-Safety-to-Governance Shift Across Organizations

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from 'Org Pivots Are Legible': Mapping the AI-Safety-to-Governance Shift Across Organizations

**Problem:** A success state where the field allocates effort wisely requires understanding whether MIRI's pivot from alignment to governance reflects a broader trend. We lack a systematic, evidence-based map of how technical safety organizations have shifted research emphasis over time.

**Direction:** Collect public outputs (blog posts, papers, agendas, job postings) from ~8-10 AI safety orgs over time and code each for emphasis: technical alignment vs governance vs evals vs policy. Use simple text classification (keyword + LLM-coded taxonomy with a fixed rubric) to chart how each org's mix shifted year-over-year, testing whether MIRI's pivot is idiosyncratic or part of a wave.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from 'the field self-corrects sensibly' shows legible effort-allocation as the precondition. This directly follows the FR68 surprising-result suggestion to analyze whether other technical orgs are pivoting like MIRI. A trend map informs funders and the strategic landscape. Public-document analysis, no lab resources.

**Relevant context:** Subfield surprising result + FR68: MIRI's 2025 pivot from alignment to governance; suggestion to analyze whether other technical orgs are making similar pivots. MIRI 'AI Governance to Avoid Extinction' agenda.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Mixed: public-doc analysis but more field-strategy than a safety lever labs ignore.
